newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns Iran it could face international bloc.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns Iran it could face international bloc.

text.p: Israel on Wednesday warned arch-foe Iran that if it did not change its ways it could face an international coalition like the force that battled Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War.
Foreign Minister David Levy, in a speech at Israel's parliament, called moderate Iranian president-elect Mohammad Khatami a man "who knows the Western world" and who could bring positive change.
Levy voiced hope Iran would alter its policies in the wake of the election.

"Israel never declared that Iran was an enemy and we would be very happy if we could see Iran integrate itself into the regional effort to reduce tension and stop terrorism, in the search for ways of cooperation and peace. That is our hope."

But Levy added, recalling the coalition of Western and Arab states that fought Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War, that the Western world would not wait forever for Tehran to halt what he said was its backing for "terrorism" and drive to destroy Israel.

"The world will not suffer the continuation of this policy. There could be an international coalition against Iran, I've already heard things in that direction, and the Western world, the free world still relates with patience and hope, to see the change so that it will not be forced to act," Levy said.
On Sunday an aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed Khatami's election but Netanyahu said it was too early to assess developments in Iran.
Commercial and military ties between Israel and Iran gave way to belligerence after the 1979 Islamic revolution.

Israel accuses Tehran of developing nuclear and other non-conventional weapons to point at the Jewish state and of arming Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas who battle Israeli troops occupying a strip in south Lebanon.
Israel also says Iran is responsible for the fate of its missing airman Ron Arad whose bomber was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. Tehran denies knowledge of his whereabouts.

"I would expect from the president-elect, the moderate, who places emphasis on citizens' rights, a man of religion, that he would bring a turning point on an issue that touches us...Ron Arad," Levy said.
